altaAutonomo.question: How do I register as self-employed (autónomo) in Spain in 2026?
altaAutonomo.answer: To register as self-employed in Spain you need three steps: register with the Tax Agency (Hacienda) using form 036 or 037, register with Social Security under the RETA scheme, and notify the town hall if you open physical premises. The whole process is free if you do it yourself and can be completed online in under an hour with a digital certificate.
altaAutonomo.cta: Need an accountant to handle it for you? Find one on MisAutónomos

cuotaAutonomos.question: How much is the self-employed Social Security contribution in 2026?
cuotaAutonomos.answer: In 2026 the self-employed contribution works in brackets based on net income: from roughly €230/month for the lowest brackets to over €590/month for the highest. New self-employed workers can opt for the flat rate of €80/month during the first year, extendable for one more year if income is low.
cuotaAutonomos.cta: Work out your exact contribution with an advisor

impuestosAutonomo.question: What taxes does a self-employed worker pay in Spain?
impuestosAutonomo.answer: A self-employed worker in Spain mainly pays income tax (IRPF, quarterly via form 130 or through 7-15% withholdings), VAT (form 303 quarterly, generally 21%), and the monthly Social Security contribution. You must also file annual summaries (form 390 and the annual income tax return, form 100).
impuestosAutonomo.cta: Talk to a specialised accountancy firm

gastosDeducibles.question: What expenses can a self-employed worker deduct?
gastosDeducibles.answer: You can deduct expenses directly tied to your activity: premises rent, utilities (with limits if you work from home, normally 30% of the 30% of the property), office supplies, a vehicle if used exclusively for work, meal allowances, training, activity-related insurance and professional association fees.
gastosDeducibles.cta: Optimise your deductions with a tax advisor

facturarAutonomo.question: How do I invoice as a self-employed worker?
facturarAutonomo.answer: A self-employed invoice must include: a sequential number, issue date, full details of issuer and recipient (name, tax ID, address), a description of the service or product, taxable base, VAT applied and total. Since 2024 electronic invoicing is mandatory between companies and self-employed workers in Spain.
facturarAutonomo.cta: Need invoicing software or an accountant?

autonomoVsSl.question: When is it better to be self-employed and when to set up an SL (limited company)?
autonomoVsSl.answer: Being self-employed is simpler and cheaper at the start (no minimum capital, simple admin). An SL makes sense when your net profit exceeds roughly €40,000-60,000 a year (corporate tax is a flat 25% versus the progressive income tax of the self-employed) or when you want to limit personal liability.
autonomoVsSl.cta: Ask an advisor which one suits you

tarifaPlana.question: What is the self-employed flat rate and who qualifies?
tarifaPlana.answer: The flat rate is a reduced contribution of €80/month for the first 12 months for new self-employed workers. It can be extended 12 more months if net income stays below the minimum wage (SMI). It is open to those who have not been registered in the previous 2 years (3 years if they already used the flat rate before).
tarifaPlana.cta: Check whether you meet the requirements

modelo130.question: When do I file form 130 and what is it for?
modelo130.answer: Form 130 is the advance income tax payment for self-employed workers under direct estimation. It is filed quarterly: by 20 April, 20 July, 20 October and 30 January of the following year. You pay 20% of the year's accumulated net profit, minus what was already paid in previous quarters.
modelo130.cta: Let an accountant file your taxes

pluriactividad.question: Can I be self-employed and an employee at the same time?
pluriactividad.answer: Yes, it's called pluriactividad. You can combine salaried employment with self-employed activity. Social Security refunds up to 50% of the self-employed contribution during the first 18 months if your salary as an employee exceeds the minimum wage (SMI).
pluriactividad.cta: Work out the refund you're entitled to

bajaAutonomo.question: How do I deregister as self-employed?
bajaAutonomo.answer: To deregister you must file the deregistration with the Tax Agency (form 036/037) and with Social Security (form TA.0521) within a maximum of 3 days from ceasing activity. Missing the deadline can lead to penalties. You are still required to file the returns for the current quarter.
bajaAutonomo.cta: Let an accountant handle your deregistration

encontrarAutonomo.question: How do I find a trustworthy self-employed professional near me?
encontrarAutonomo.answer: To find a reliable professional check that they are registered under RETA (you can ask for the certificate), have liability insurance, reviews from other clients, a detailed written quote before starting, and always issue an invoice. On MisAutónomos every professional is verified.
encontrarAutonomo.cta: Find verified professionals in my area

cuantoCobra.question: How much does a self-employed professional charge per hour in Spain in 2026?
cuantoCobra.answer: Rates vary a lot by trade: a plumber or electrician bills between €30 and €50/hour, a freelance developer between €35 and €80/hour, a designer between €25 and €60/hour, an accountancy firm between €60 and €150/hour, a self-employed lawyer between €80 and €200/hour. Always ask for a fixed quote to avoid surprises.
cuantoCobra.cta: Get free quotes from several professionals

facturaObligatoria.question: Is a self-employed professional required to give me an invoice?
facturaObligatoria.answer: Yes, every self-employed worker is legally required to issue an invoice for each service provided. If they refuse, you can report it to the Tax Agency. The invoice is your legal guarantee that the service was provided and, where applicable, lets you deduct VAT if you are a company or self-employed.
facturaObligatoria.cta: Work with professionals who always invoice

noTermina.question: What can I do if a professional doesn't finish the job or disappears?
noTermina.answer: Gather all the evidence (contract, signed quotes, messages, payments), send a burofax with a deadline to comply, and if there's no response you can file a consumer complaint (if you're a private individual) or a lawsuit. To avoid this risk, always hire professionals with verified reviews and never pay 100% up front.
noTermina.cta: Hire verified professionals with a guarantee

autonomoVsEmpresa.question: Is a self-employed professional cheaper than a company?
autonomoVsEmpresa.answer: Generally yes, a self-employed professional tends to be cheaper because they have lower overheads. But there are important differences: a company usually offers more formal guarantees, greater capacity for large projects and continuity. For one-off and mid-sized jobs, a self-employed professional is the most cost-effective option.
autonomoVsEmpresa.cta: Compare quotes from professionals in your area

queEs.question: What is MisAutónomos and how does it work?
queEs.answer: MisAutónomos is a platform that connects clients with verified self-employed professionals across Spain. Clients post what they need, professionals send quotes, and after comparing, the client picks the one they prefer. For professionals it's a way to win new clients without spending on advertising.

esGratis.question: Is it free to sign up to MisAutónomos as a professional?
esGratis.answer: Yes, signing up as a professional on MisAutónomos is completely free with no commitment. You can create your professional profile, receive quote requests and work with clients without paying anything. We offer optional paid plans (Visibility and Ads+) for professionals who want to stand out in search results.
esGratis.cta: Sign me up for free as a professional

planes.question: What do the Visibility Plan and the Ads+ Plan include?
planes.answer: The Visibility Plan highlights your profile in search results and gives you access to visit statistics. The Ads+ Plan includes all of that plus active advertising campaigns managed by our team, priority ranking in your area and dedicated support. Both plans can be cancelled at any time.

verificacion.question: How are professionals verified on MisAutónomos?
verificacion.answer: We verify every professional by checking their RETA registration, tax ID (NIF/DNI), real contact details and, in regulated trades, their qualification or licence. Verified profiles show a specific badge. This gives clients peace of mind and sets serious professionals apart.

solicitudes.question: How do I receive quote requests on MisAutónomos?
solicitudes.answer: When a client posts a need in your category and area, you get an alert by email and in your platform dashboard. You decide whether to send a quote. The more complete your profile (photo, description, work examples, reviews), the more requests you'll receive. Complete profiles receive up to 5 times more requests.

privacy.seoDescription: Learn how we protect your personal data at MisAutónomos
privacy.title: Privacy Policy

controller.title: 1. Data Controller
controller.text: MisAutónomos is responsible for processing your personal data. Our commitment is to protect your privacy and ensure the security of your information.

dataCollected.title: 2. Data We Collect
dataCollected.text: We collect the following information: (a) Identification data: name, email, phone, (b) Professional data: CIF/NIF, service categories, location, (c) Usage data: platform interactions, messages, favorites, (d) Payment data: billing information managed by Stripe.

purpose.title: 3. Purpose of Processing
purpose.text: We use your data to: (a) Provide and improve our services, (b) Facilitate connection between clients and professionals, (c) Process payments and subscriptions, (d) Send service-related communications, (e) Comply with legal obligations.

legalBasis.title: 4. Legal Basis
legalBasis.text: We process your data based on: (a) Performance of service contract, (b) User consent, (c) Legitimate interest of MisAutónomos, (d) Compliance with legal obligations.

sharing.title: 5. Data Sharing
sharing.text: Your data may be shared with: (a) Professionals/clients you interact with, (b) Stripe for payment processing, (c) Technical service providers (hosting, email), (d) Authorities when legally required.

retention.title: 6. Data Retention
retention.text: We retain your data while: (a) You maintain your active account, (b) It's necessary to comply with legal obligations, (c) Pending claims exist. After deleting your account, your data will be erased within 30 days.

rights.title: 7. Your Rights
rights.text: You have the right to: (a) Access your personal data, (b) Rectify incorrect data, (c) Request deletion of your data, (d) Object to processing, (e) Data portability, (f) Revoke consent. To exercise your rights, contact: soporte@misautonomos.es

security.title: 8. Security
security.text: We implement technical and organizational measures to protect your data against unauthorized access, alteration, disclosure or destruction. We use SSL encryption, secure authentication and protected storage.

cookies.title: 9. Cookies
cookies.text: We use cookies to improve your experience. You can manage cookie preferences in our Cookie Policy.

changes.title: 10. Policy Changes
changes.text: We may update this policy occasionally. We will notify you about significant changes by email or notice on the platform.

privacy.contactLead: To exercise your rights or privacy inquiries

terms.seoDescription: Read our terms and conditions for using the MisAutónomos platform
terms.title: Terms and Conditions

acceptance.title: 1. Acceptance of Terms
acceptance.text: By accessing and using MisAutónomos, you agree to be legally bound by these terms and conditions. If you do not agree with any part of these terms, you should not use our services.

service.title: 2. Service Description
service.text: MisAutónomos is a digital platform that connects clients with verified freelance professionals in Spain. We facilitate contact between both parties but are not responsible for the quality, safety or legality of services provided by professionals.

accounts.title: 3. User Registration and Accounts
accounts.text: To use certain services, you must create an account providing accurate and up-to-date information. You are responsible for maintaining the confidentiality of your account and password, and for all activities that occur under your account.

proObligations.title: 4. Professional Obligations
proObligations.text: Professionals who register on MisAutónomos must: (a) Be legally authorized to work as freelancers in Spain, (b) Provide truthful and verifiable information, (c) Keep their profile and availability updated, (d) Comply with all applicable laws and regulations.

clientObligations.title: 5. Client Obligations
clientObligations.text: Clients using MisAutónomos must: (a) Provide accurate information about required services, (b) Communicate respectfully with professionals, (c) Comply with agreements established with professionals.

subscriptions.title: 6. Subscriptions and Payments
subscriptions.text: Professionals must maintain an active subscription to appear in searches. Subscriptions renew automatically unless canceled before the renewal date. Payments are processed through Stripe. All prices include VAT when applicable.

userContent.title: 7. User Content
userContent.text: You retain all rights to content you publish on MisAutónomos. However, you grant us a worldwide, non-exclusive, royalty-free license to use, reproduce and display such content in connection with the operation of our services.

intellectualProperty.title: 8. Intellectual Property
intellectualProperty.text: All content on MisAutónomos, including but not limited to text, graphics, logos, icons, images and software, is property of MisAutónomos or its licensors and is protected by Spanish and international intellectual property laws.

liability.title: 9. Limitation of Liability
liability.text: MisAutónomos acts only as an intermediary. We are not responsible for: (a) Quality, safety or legality of services offered, (b) Truthfulness of professional profiles, (c) Direct or indirect damages arising from platform use, (d) Disputes between clients and professionals.

termination.title: 10. Suspension and Termination
termination.text: We reserve the right to suspend or terminate your account if: (a) You violate these terms, (b) You provide false information, (c) You use the platform for illegal activities, (d) You abuse or harass other users.

modifications.title: 11. Modifications
modifications.text: We may modify these terms at any time. Changes will take effect immediately after publication on the platform. Continued use of the service constitutes acceptance of the modified terms.

law.title: 12. Applicable Law and Jurisdiction
law.text: These terms shall be governed and interpreted in accordance with the laws of Spain. Any dispute shall be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of Madrid, Spain.
